title: Kingdom of Spain
capsule: The Kingdom of Spain emerged in 1516 when Charles I (Holy Roman Emperor Charles V) united the crowns of Castile and Aragon under Habsburg rule, creating the first major European composite monarchy with simultaneous dominion over the Americas, the Italian states, and the Low Countries. The sixteenth and seventeenth centuries constituted Spain's imperial apogee: silver from Potosí and New Spain financed European hegemony under Philip II (r. 1556–1598), whose realm encompassed Portugal and its empire after 1580. The War of the Spanish Succession (1701–1714) replaced the Habsburgs with the Bourbon dynasty and stripped Spain of its Italian and Low Country territories, while the Napoleonic invasion of 1808 triggered the collapse of most of the American empire by the 1820s. The constitutional monarchy persists to the present, having transitioned from Francoism to democracy after 1975.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Peninsular boundaries of Spain are precisely documented by treaty from the 16th century; colonial and overseas territorial extents are well-attested through administrative records but varied rapidly with conquest and independence movements.
